input.quote: 28.2 The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 already selects New York law (preferred element 1 met verbatim), and there is no arbitration provision anywhere in the Agreement. However, the exclusivity of the New York County forum in 28.2 is undercut by the retained carve-out allowing either Party to sue for temporary injunctive relief "in another court with jurisdiction"; an exclusive-jurisdiction element is not met while an another-court carve-out survives, and the fallback (Delaware, California, or England and Wales law and the corresponding courts) is inapplicable to this New York bargain. We therefore made the single shortest change — deleting the carve-out sentence — leaving 28.1, the CISG exclusion, and the 28.3 pre-filing process untouched.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
mappings.quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.

ops.oldText: Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the carve-out permitting suits for injunctive relief in other courts so that the state and federal courts in New York County are genuinely exclusive, consistent with our governing-law and venue position. New York law in 28.1 is unchanged.
proposal.summary: Delete another-court carve-out to make New York County jurisdiction exclusive.
